title: Satoshi's Countdown
one_liner: Race a simulated self-improving AI against SHA-256 to see when it could theoretically crack and drain the original Bitcoin wallet.
speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
context: Chamath argued crypto is capped because recursive AI self-improvement could eventually be pointed at breaking SHA-256 to drain Satoshi's original wallet, then short Bitcoin.
demo: Visitor sets an 'AI compute doubling rate' slider next to a fixed 2^256 keyspace bar; an animated progress bar races toward 'wallet drained,' with a readout translating the slider into a dramatized crack-year estimate, plus a toggle comparing classical versus hypothetical quantum-assisted rates.
data_plan: Simulated, clearly labeled log-scale model of compute growth versus keyspace size; no real cryptographic claims.
risks: Must disclaim this is dramatized fiction, not a real cryptographic timeline — brute-forcing SHA-256 is considered infeasible for any foreseeable computer; mislabeling could spread misinformation.
